item_description: A family of manufacturing processes that builds objects layer by layer from a digital model.
item_facts: The formal term is additive manufacturing.
Different processes use materials such as polymers, metals or resins.
No single inventor created all forms of 3D printing; key methods emerged over time.
needs_review: Verify process terminology and invention history; avoid a single-inventor claim.

item_description: A powered, fixed-wing aircraft capable of controlled flight through the air.
item_facts: The Wright brothers made a powered, controlled airplane flight in 1903 at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
Earlier gliders and experiments contributed to aviation development.
The term 'first airplane' depends on how powered and controlled flight is defined.
needs_review: Verify priority claims and terminology through aviation history sources.

item_description: The Global Positioning System, a U.S. satellite navigation system that provides positioning and timing information.
item_facts: GPS uses signals from satellites and receiver measurements to estimate location.
It is one of several global navigation satellite systems.
Reliable positioning generally requires signals from multiple satellites and suitable geometry.
needs_review: Verify technical explanation and distinguish GPS from other GNSS systems using official sources.

item_description: A semiconductor device that combines multiple electronic components on a single piece of material, usually silicon.
item_facts: Integrated circuits are also called microchips or chips.
Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce independently developed important early integrated-circuit designs.
Modern chips can contain billions of transistors.
needs_review: Verify invention chronology and avoid oversimplifying independent contributions.

item_description: A global network of interconnected networks that communicate using the Internet Protocol suite.
item_facts: The Internet is distinct from the World Wide Web, which is a service that runs on it.
ARPANET was an important precursor network.
The Internet developed through many technical and institutional contributions, not a single invention event.
needs_review: Verify historical milestones and distinguish Internet from Web.

item_description: A device that produces light through stimulated emission, typically in a narrow and coherent beam.
item_facts: The word laser is an acronym for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation.
The first working laser was demonstrated by Theodore Maiman in 1960.
Laser light can be visible, infrared or ultraviolet depending on the device.
needs_review: Verify scientific wording and historical priority using technical and historical sources.

item_description: An electric lamp that converts electrical energy into visible light; many inventors contributed to its development.
item_facts: Early incandescent lamps predate Thomas Edison’s commercially successful systems.
Edison and his team improved lamp design and electric lighting infrastructure in the late 19th century.
Modern lighting also includes fluorescent and LED technologies.
needs_review: Avoid saying Edison single-handedly invented the light bulb; verify invention chronology.

item_description: A rechargeable battery technology in which lithium ions move between electrodes during charge and discharge.
item_facts: Lithium-ion batteries are used in phones, laptops and electric vehicles.
John Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino were awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work enabling the battery.
Battery chemistry and performance differ among cell designs.
needs_review: Verify scientific description and accurately represent the multiple contributors.

item_description: An appliance that heats food using microwave-frequency electromagnetic energy.
item_facts: Microwaves cause polar molecules, especially water, to rotate and dissipate energy as heat.
Percy Spencer’s work at Raytheon led to the first commercial microwave oven.
Microwave ovens do not make food radioactive.
needs_review: Verify mechanism wording and invention history from scientific and museum sources.

item_description: A computer designed for use by an individual, emerging through many developments in electronics, software and affordable hardware.
item_facts: Early personal computers became available in the 1970s.
The 1977 systems from Apple, Commodore and Tandy helped popularize home computing.
There is no single universally accepted first personal computer.
needs_review: First-PC claims depend on definition; verify specific historical claims.

item_description: A machine for applying ink to paper or other material, enabling books and documents to be reproduced at scale.
item_facts: Movable-type printing existed in East Asia before Gutenberg’s press.
Johannes Gutenberg developed a influential movable-metal-type printing system in Europe in the 15th century.
Printing technologies developed independently in different regions.
needs_review: Avoid Eurocentric claims that Gutenberg invented printing globally; verify chronological detail.

item_description: A technology for transmitting information using electromagnetic waves, developed through contributions from many inventors and scientists.
item_facts: Radio communication relies on electromagnetic radiation at radio frequencies.
Guglielmo Marconi helped develop practical wireless telegraphy.
The history of radio includes independent contributions by multiple researchers.
needs_review: Priority and invention claims are disputed; verify a multi-contributor historical account.

item_description: A machine that removes heat from an enclosed space to keep its contents cool.
item_facts: Most household refrigerators use a vapor-compression refrigeration cycle.
Refrigeration systems were developed over many decades by multiple inventors.
Refrigerators slow many forms of food spoilage but do not sterilize food.
needs_review: Verify refrigeration mechanism and historical timeline with technical sources.

item_description: A heat engine that converts the energy of steam into mechanical work.
item_facts: Thomas Newcomen built an early practical atmospheric steam engine in the early 18th century.
James Watt’s improvements made steam engines more efficient and adaptable.
Steam power contributed to industrialization but did not have a single inventor.
needs_review: Verify invention chronology and avoid attributing the engine to one person alone.

item_description: A device that transmits voice and other sound over distance using electrical or digital signals.
item_facts: Alexander Graham Bell received a U.S. telephone patent in 1876.
Several inventors developed related voice-transmission devices around the same period.
Modern telephones convert voice to digital data and operate through network infrastructure.
needs_review: Telephone priority is disputed; represent the patent history and competing inventors accurately.

item_description: A system for transmitting and displaying moving images and sound, developed through mechanical and electronic technologies.
item_facts: Early television experiments used both mechanical scanning and electronic systems.
Philo Farnsworth and Vladimir Zworykin were among key contributors to electronic television.
Television technology has evolved from analog broadcast to digital and internet delivery.
needs_review: Verify invention chronology and credit multiple contributors.

item_description: A semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electrical signals and the basic building block of modern digital electronics.
item_facts: The first working point-contact transistor was demonstrated at Bell Labs in 1947.
John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley received the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for transistor research.
Billions of transistors can be integrated into a modern processor.
needs_review: Verify historical and technical details using Bell Labs and Nobel sources.

item_description: A method of training the immune system to recognize a pathogen using a vaccine.
item_facts: Edward Jenner’s 1796 smallpox vaccination work was an important milestone in modern immunization.
Variolation existed earlier in several regions and is distinct from vaccination.
Vaccines use different technologies and do not all work in the same way.
needs_review: Avoid a single-origin narrative; verify global history and technical claims with medical-history sources.

item_description: A system of linked documents and resources accessed over the Internet using web browsers and protocols.
item_facts: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the Web at CERN in 1989.
The Web uses technologies including URLs, HTTP and HTML.
The Internet is the underlying network; the Web is one service that uses it.
needs_review: Verify proposal and implementation dates using CERN historical materials.

item_description: A medical and scientific imaging technique that uses X-rays to reveal structures inside an object.
item_facts: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895.
X-rays are a form of ionizing electromagnetic radiation.
Different imaging methods, including radiography and CT, use X-rays in distinct ways.
needs_review: Verify history and radiation terminology with medical and scientific sources.
